project_policy: Do not ingest a source until the specific work's rights, license, attribution obligations, and redistribution implications have been verified and recorded.

priority_areas.subject: Programming fundamentals
priority_areas.recommendation: Use selected Python documentation pages and examples with provenance, version, and PSF-2.0 notices recorded; exclude embedded third-party material unless separately cleared.

candidate_source.name: Python 3 Documentation
candidate_source.license_basis: The official documentation states that Python software and documentation are licensed under PSF License Version 2, and that examples and recipes from Python 3.8.6 onward are dual-licensed under PSF-2.0 and Zero-Clause BSD.

priority_areas.subject: Computer science, mathematics, reasoning, and explanations
priority_areas.recommendation: Author original lessons and worked examples with subject-matter review; obtain written rights-holder permission and explicitly release each source under CC0-1.0 or CC-BY-4.0 before ingestion.

candidate_source.name: QuantaAI-created material
candidate_source.license_basis: Future original material only; the creator or rights holder must document the selected license and permission.

priority_areas.subject: Educational question-answer pairs
priority_areas.recommendation: Create source-grounded questions and answers from approved materials, keep citations and source-document hashes, and require human verification before marking items approved.

candidate_source.name: Human-authored, source-grounded Q&A
candidate_source.license_basis: The author or rights holder must explicitly license the new work and verify each answer against an approved source.

priority_areas.subject: General knowledge and science
priority_areas.recommendation: No source is currently cleared. Select specific works with explicit CC0-1.0 or CC-BY-4.0 terms and source-level attribution; do not infer rights from free access or government affiliation.

ingestion_gates: Record source title, owner/author, original location, source URL, exact license identifier and URL, retrieval/version details, reviewer, verification date, and evidence.
Exclude sources with unknown terms, non-commercial or no-derivatives restrictions, unclear third-party content, or missing attribution rights.
Run exact and near-duplicate detection and assign shared-content leakage groups wholly to one split.
Have a subject-matter reviewer assess accuracy, quality, and Q&A references.
Stage data under data/ingestion_runs; never mutate the current splits, tokenizer, or checkpoints automatically.

preconditions: Resolve source rights for every item used; do not treat the current unknown-license corpus as approved.
Expand the corpus and create a multi-document validation split with subject coverage.
Review and freeze the evaluation set before any final test evaluation.
recommended_next_training_configuration.rationale: A bounded follow-up pilot is appropriate only after permission and dataset quality are resolved. It should test optimization stability on a more representative train/validation set, not claim language-generation quality.
